title: compose-preview-known-differences/v1
description: The committed known-difference document, `.design-parity/known-differences.json`. This file pins the document's SHAPE only. The rules that decide a verdict — id and path safety, the budget preflight, the mask's IHDR encoding, the animation check, hash normalisation, the five gates, the status precedence, the one entry per acceptance in `statuses` and the ordering of `validationFailures` (`statuses` is an unordered map and is given no ordering) — cannot be expressed in JSON Schema and are normative in docs/design/COMPONENT_PARITY_WORKFLOW.md §4, implemented in known-differences.mjs and pinned by fixtures/known-differences/. A document that validates here can still be refused; nothing that fails here is ever accepted.

id.description: A stable identifier doing double duty as a map key and a path segment, which is why it is constrained three ways — the character class here, the reserved map keys (`__proto__`, `constructor`, `prototype`) and both dot names, neither of which JSON Schema can express.

issue.description: Mandatory per acceptance, not unique to one: several acceptances legitimately point at one tracking issue, and the issue is closable only once every one of them resolves. Compared as canonical owner/repo/number, never as the URL string.

variant.description: Axes only. Overrides live in `overrides` and nowhere else — one fact, one field.

overrides.description: The whole normalised map the render lane receives, with absence meaning 'no overrides'. Matching is exact over the whole set: every key the render lane accepts is in scope, including `knob.<key>` and `rc.<name>`, because a key that did not affect the render would not be in the map.

plane.description: The canonical plane the mask was authored against. `normalisedBoxes` falls back to the full canvas below MIN_BOX_COVERAGE, and the reference's sha256 does not pin which side of that threshold the pair fell — so the discriminant and the resolved box are recorded rather than re-derived.

candidateTolerance.description: Per-pixel 8-bit channel distance for the candidate gate and the resolution test. Integer, and the integer requirement is normative: JSON has one number type, so 0.5 sails through a range-only check in JavaScript and is rejected by a Kotlin Int field.

element.description: Optional. An acceptance with no `element` key at all is the geometric case; one that CAN name an element must, because the gate is what separates 'the glyph disappeared' from 'the glyph is still the wrong colour'.

kind.description: v1 defines exactly one identifying kind. A `producer` kind was cut because nothing can currently carry it, and a selector kind with no authoring path is worse than absent — it reads as available.

tag.description: The testTag, matched anywhere in the tree; the ancestor path is irrelevant because the resolver never walks it.

bounds.description: The authoring-time baseline in canonical-plane coordinates. Required, not derivable: the evaluator otherwise holds only the element's current bounds, and the mask is not a usable stand-in because it commonly covers one part of the selected element.

tolerance.description: A fraction of the SMALLER baseline dimension, compared against the MAXIMUM of the four edge displacements, with `>` so a displacement exactly at tolerance passes.

artifactPath.description: Relative to the acceptance's own directory under .design-parity/known-differences/<id>/. Contained AND portable: segments of [A-Za-z0-9._-] joined by /, so no backslash, no # or ? or %, and no whitespace — a contained path can still name different files on either side of the contract.

recordedHash.description: Exactly 64 lowercase hex characters. We cannot constrain what a producer publishes upstream — a SERVED hash may be spelled loosely and is normalised before comparison — but we can refuse two spellings of our own fields.
